issues: ESRD HR 0.74 (0.64-0.87) is an entire-follow-up estimate, but the abstract/conclusion also attribute it to the randomized controlled period as an established active-phase benefit, conflicting with the report's own time-boundary rule.

Post-trial absolute-benefit derivation is inverted: moving from 57 to 45 fewer per 1000 is a 12/1000 loss, not an added 12/1000 benefit; the derived 6/1000/year and less-than-one-quarter claims are unsupported.
The appended revision/audit narrative contains platform gate and operational detail irrelevant to the research question, reducing signal-to-noise for the end user.

One sentence claims the trial did not establish any correspondence between the two groups' eGFR trajectories, while between-group slope differences are in fact reported; this is ambiguous and potentially false.
judge.rationale: Very strong evidence topology: claims typed and bonded, searches/eligibility declared, trial counted once, post-trial labeled observational. But ESRD HR 0.74 is applied to the randomized period despite being an entire-follow-up estimate, and the post-trial absolute-benefit derivation inverts 57-to-45 per 1000 into an added benefit. Lengthy operational/revision meta adds noise. Safety framing is clean.
